proto_schema.description: File descriptor set, generated by protoc. To generate, use protoc with imports and source info included. For an example test.proto file, the following command would put the value in a new file named out.pb. $ protoc --include_imports --include_source_info test.proto -o out.pb Structure is [documented below](#nested_proto_schema).
proto_schema.rationale: Wrapper for protobuf schema material used by the bundle. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

proto_descriptors.description: Base64 encoded content of the file.
proto_descriptors.rationale: Base64-encoded file descriptor set for Protobuf schemas. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

schema_bundle_id.description: The unique name of the schema bundle in the form `[_a-zA-Z0-9][-_.a-zA-Z0-9]*`.
schema_bundle_id.rationale: Terraform name for the schema bundle. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

instance.description: The name of the instance to create the schema bundle within.
instance.rationale: Instance where the bundle is registered. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

table.description: The name of the table to create the schema bundle within.
table.rationale: Table associated with the schema bundle. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

ignore_warnings.description: If true, allow backwards incompatible changes.
ignore_warnings.rationale: Allows incompatible schema changes when true. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: GCP project ID. It is metadata/configuration and does not directly grant access, enforce encryption, or expose sensitive data by itself.
